solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Walker may use this trick to take in silly sap

indicators.note: to take something in is to receive it inside, so one piece goes within another
silly means foolish or muddled, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: a knack is a trick or special skill
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A walker plays a trick on some gullible fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sap' reads as a gullible dupe, but it is only three letters to jumble, placed inside the trick word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiker or rambler carries a bag strapped to the back holding kit, so the cryptic description points to that pack.

clue.text: Kafka’s first novel cutting if not authentic

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word it is attached to
something cutting into another thing sits inside it, splitting it apart

blocks.note: the initial letter of the author's name
She is the famous adventure novel by H. Rider Haggard
'or' can mean 'if not', as in 'hurry or you'll be late'

explanation.surface: A literary remark that Kafka's first novel is inauthentic unless something is true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' is not an anagram signal but a specific book: She, the Victorian adventure by H. Rider Haggard, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Kosher literally means ritually fit under Jewish dietary law, and informally means genuine or legitimate.

clue.text: Thrash metal about right for this band

indicators.note: to thrash is to beat violently, so the letters are knocked into a new order
about means around, so one set of letters surrounds the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A thrash metal band sounding just right to a rock fan.
explanation.walkthrough: Thrash metal is a genre, and 'band' seems to mean a group of musicians, but it is a band worn on the arm; the scrambled METAL goes around R.
explanation.definitionFit: An armlet is a ring or strip of material worn round the upper arm, so it is a kind of band.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory hearing air Holst composed drinking whiskey

indicators.note: a composed piece has been put together, so these letters are arranged anew
whatever is drinking takes something in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A disappointing listen to a tune Holst wrote while drinking whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' belongs to the definition as a court hearing, not a listening; Gustav Holst was an English composer, which makes 'composed' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A show trial is a staged judicial proceeding with a predetermined verdict, a travesty of a fair court hearing.

clue.text: Emptied ideal sauce into soup — this adds flavour

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only its outside letters
into puts one thing inside another, placing letters within a larger word

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
sauce and lip both mean cheeky impudence
chowder is a thick soup, often of seafood

explanation.surface: A cook tips out a perfect sauce into the soup to improve its taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' tempts as a cooking word, but it means cheek, as in 'less of your sauce'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground dried hot peppers make a spice that cooks sprinkle in to give food heat and taste.

clue.text: Where to pray about games installed in rogue computer

indicators.note: something installed in a machine is fitted inside it

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
HAL 9000 is the murderous computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey
PE, physical education, is school games

explanation.surface: Someone praying about games software loaded onto a malfunctioning computer.
explanation.walkthrough: The rogue computer is the one from Kubrick's 2001 that turns on its crew; games are school PE lessons, and about is circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small place of worship, or a room within a larger building set aside for prayer.

clue.text: In China, majority group cry for attention in Asian city

blocks.note: the Han are China's dominant ethnic group
'Oi!' is a shout to get someone to notice you

explanation.surface: China's largest ethnic group calls out for notice in an Asian metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In China' is part of the description of the Han, not a container signal. OI is British slang for 'hey!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Endless calm around setter up for a bit of setting

indicators.note: without an end, a word drops its final letter
in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards
around means surrounding, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: placate, to calm, minus its last letter
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A setter trying to stay calm about a bit of typesetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calm' is a verb here: PLACATE. 'Setting' seems to be about the setter's craft but means a table setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A table setting is one diner's cutlery, crockery and mat, so the mat under the plate is one part of it.

clue.text: Instigator of luminarism, as well as visionary artist

indicators.note: the instigator starts things off, so the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: the initial letter of the word
as well as means and
a seer is a visionary, a prophet

explanation.surface: The founder of a painting movement who was also a visionary artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Luminism is a real painting style, so the surface reads as art history. Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter of animals who also sculpted the Trafalgar Square lions.
explanation.definitionFit: Landseer was a celebrated nineteenth-century English painter, so he is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Maybe Arabic circles love analysing signs and symbols

indicators.note: to circle something is to go right round it, enclosing it

blocks.note: Arabic is one of the Semitic languages
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Scholars of Arabic love working out signs and symbols, perhaps in the script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circles' looks like a noun (groups of scholars) but is a verb: SEMITIC goes round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Semiotics is the study of signs and how they carry meaning, and the adjective describes that kind of study.

clue.text: Way to transport goods around island without success

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: goods can travel in a van
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A delivery firm ferries goods round an island without making any money.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'way' is a phrase rather than a single word: 'in van' is how the goods go, and I is put into the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in vain means doing it fruitlessly, to no purpose or effect.

clue.text: Business people admitting ordeal is challenging

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: CO is short for company, a business
a nation is a people
a test is an ordeal or trial

explanation.surface: Business folk concede that an ordeal is difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Challenging' looks like an adjective meaning difficult, but it is a verbal noun: the act of challenging.
explanation.definitionFit: Contestation is the act of disputing or calling into question, which is what challenging something means.

clue.text: What happens in 11, 12 and also in 17, written out?

indicators.note: the numbers must be spelt in words, and the letters sit within those spellings

blocks.note: spelt out, the letters run across the join of eleven and twelve
spelt out, seventeen holds the same run of letters

explanation.surface: A self-referential puzzle asking what is going on in three of this grid's own entries.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like grid references to other clues, but they are just numbers to spell out: elEVEN Twelve and sEVENTeen both contain EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence, something that takes place or comes to pass.

clue.text: E.g. ladies and gents hiding pants showing eccentricity

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the ladies and the gents are loos, British public toilets
to pant for something is to long for it, as is to pine

explanation.surface: Public toilets with underwear concealed in them, which seems rather odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is British for underpants, which suits the toilets, but here it is a verb, yearns.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy is informal for crazy or odd, so the noun describes being eccentric or peculiar.

clue.text: Where papers are kept in detective’s investigation about plot

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: DI (detective inspector) with 's, then case, an investigation
a patch is a small plot of land

explanation.surface: Documents held in the files of a detective's inquiry into a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' suggests a conspiracy in a crime story but is a garden patch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch case is a flat case for carrying official documents, so papers are stored in it.

clue.text: Dislike eating meat I cooked? It’s a source of iron

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another
cooked means altered or fiddled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to hate is to dislike strongly
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who hates eating the meat they cooked is told it is full of iron.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about diet, where meat is a food source of iron; the answer is a mineral instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Haematite is a reddish iron oxide mineral and one of the principal ores mined for the metal.

clue.text: Pupil once expelled after losing head complained

indicators.note: after says which piece follows the other in the finished word
losing its head means the first letter drops off

blocks.note: an old boy, OB, is a former pupil of a school
ejected means thrown out, expelled

explanation.surface: A former pupil, thrown out after being decapitated, protested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil once expelled' reads as one expelled schoolboy, but it splits into two pieces; old boy is the British term for a former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: To object is to protest or voice disapproval, so the past tense matches complained.

clue.text: Reportedly get The Kinks out of distress

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken or told, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: to straighten is to remove kinks or bends

explanation.surface: Rescuing the rock band The Kinks from trouble, as the news tells it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kinks were a 1960s British rock band, but here kinks are just twists to be smoothed out.
explanation.definitionFit: To straiten is to restrict or put into hardship, especially financial, which is to cause distress.

clue.text: Drudge changing bather’s towel

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A servant swaps a swimmer's towel for a fresh one.
explanation.walkthrough: The drudge seems to be the one changing the towel, but 'changing' only signals the letter shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle-washer, as in chief cook and bottle-washer, is a menial who does all the lowly chores.

clue.text: Furniture from person a crossword is compiled for?

definitions.text: person a crossword is compiled for?

blocks.note: first meaning: a seat for two or more people

blocks.clueFragment: person a crossword is compiled for?
blocks.note: second meaning, whimsical: one for whom a puzzle is set, as an employee is one who is employed

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented word: a setter sets, so the solver would be the -ee who is set for.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a sofa, a piece of upholstered seating, and the made-up sense follows the pattern of employer and employee.

clue.text: Incentive to turn up during motor racing

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the letters lie inside the words that follow
in a down entry, turning up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: the letters run backwards across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A prize to tempt drivers to show up at a motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' seems to mean arrive, but in a down clue it asks for letters read upwards: motoR RACing, backwards, gives CARROT.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot, as in carrot and stick, is a reward dangled to motivate someone, like the vegetable held before a donkey.

clue.text: Rash head of Armenia gets behind old, patriotic song

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter
getting behind means coming after, so this piece goes at the end

blocks.note: ex means former, old
a national anthem is a patriotic song
the initial letter of the country

explanation.surface: Armenia's impetuous leader backs a former national anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like an adjective describing the leader, but it is the noun defined.
explanation.definitionFit: An exanthema is a medical term for a skin eruption accompanying diseases such as measles, a widespread rash.

clue.text: Lake house in Thanet occasionally abandoned

indicators.note: letters dropped every so often leave only every other one
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters
HO is an abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A lakeside home on the Isle of Thanet left empty from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Thanet is an area of north-east Kent in England. Take its odd letters and put HO inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Tahoe is a large freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada on the California–Nevada border.

clue.text: Assistant used on-line articles about classical law

indicators.note: about means around, so these pieces surround another

blocks.note: two indefinite articles, A and A
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: An internet helper writes articles on Roman law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classical' points to Latin, the classical language.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexa is Amazon's voice-controlled virtual helper, which works through an internet connection.

clue.text: Little time followed by long year

indicators.note: followed by sets the order, one piece coming before the next

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to long for something is to itch for it
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A short time is followed by a lengthy year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' and 'long' look like describers of time, but 'Little' is the definition and 'long' is a verb, to itch.
explanation.definitionFit: Titchy is British slang for very small, from Little Tich, a tiny music-hall comedian.

clue.text: Forbidding nurse to bind hip

indicators.note: to bind something is to wrap round it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: a sister is a senior nurse in British hospitals
hip and in both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: A stern nurse refusing to bandage a patient's hip joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbidding' looks like a verb (prohibiting) in the hospital scene, but it is the adjective meaning menacing, and 'hip' means trendy, not the joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister and forbidding are both adjectives describing something threatening or ominous in appearance.

clue.text: Someone refusing to accept / old money

blocks.note: first meaning: one who denies something, pronounced de-NYE-er
second meaning: a small old French coin, pronounced DEN-ee-ay

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are spelt alike but said differently; the second is also a unit of fineness for yarn and stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: One who denies is a refuser or rejecter, and the denier was a low-value coin used in medieval France.

clue.text: Returns from Bury St Edmunds, initially going inside

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter is taken
something going inside is placed within the other letters

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
taken as written
the initial letter of the name

explanation.surface: Coming back from the Suffolk town of Bury St Edmunds.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury St Edmunds is a market town in Suffolk, England; its name splits into a verb, an abbreviation and a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest is the money earned on savings or investment, so it is the financial return on capital.
